commits.message:
Play the validation-trace dispute runner to conviction at the deepest admitted trace

The failing event's script runs to the per-transaction memory cap before it
fails (394,860 steps, bisection depth 19). Two defenders, the operator's thread
on the bisection's longest path and the successor's to the redeemer field's
canonical-decode step, are bisected, resolved through one-step and closed; the
case closes Convicted with the bond back. One file observes a 13,623-byte
redeemer field inline through the compute arm, with an honest-block negative;
the other reads a 13,624-byte field through a published copy and the machine
arm. Every move lands within the transaction limits at its real fee.

Stop proposing a lost-defense slash past its deadline

Once the defender's bond unlock has passed, the receipt slash is no longer
due: the run raises no unbuilt or unfunded alarm for it and stops under
defender-won. A node that names no unlock, or cannot be read, stands on
the case's own bound (started_at + D_case + P); when that cannot be read
either the slash is not due, and the read failure is logged once.

The raw-L1 terminal derivation now takes the case id from the record's
own transaction (the case token beside its bond marker), so a header with
more than one case still derives, and takes a receipt slash as the end of
the operator's bond only when it was included before the removal.

Tests: past-unlock rows for the unbuilt and unfunded slash, an
unknown-deadline row, a restart row where another watcher's slash lands
while our process is stopped at its submit, a second-case row and a
slash-after-removal row. Shared lost-defense helpers move to a support
module; a stale comment is corrected.

Alert once when a data directory still holds the old layout's in-flight proofs

An in-place upgrade over an old-layout data directory starts, but the
per-proof fault-proofs/ journals and the handoff and abandonment funding
tables are never read, so in-flight proofs from that layout are dropped.
The warning text said their rows live in the new databases, and the README
said ignoring them did not discard durable state; neither was true.

At startup the watcher now logs one error-level
legacy_proofs_not_carried_over alert naming the non-empty fault-proofs/
directory and each legacy funding table holding rows, and still starts.
The legacy journal warning and the README now say the old journals are
never imported, list fault-proofs/, and state that the launch deployment
starts with a fresh data directory.

Delete a settled orphan reservation so a returning objective is funded again

An orphan settle left the reservation released under its decision digest.
When the header came back after the settle (a rollback shallower than
release finality, or the documented race between the eligibility check
and the settle), the objective was admitted again under the same decision,
met the released reservation, could not reserve or prepare, and was
quarantined.

The settle now deletes the reservation with its rows in the same
transaction, so the inputs return to the wallet and a returning objective
plans a fresh reservation.

Prove own thread custody from the chain again after total state loss

A watcher that loses its whole data directory in the middle of a proof
thread and restarts with the same keys could never spend its own thread
output again: its funding store no longer held the output's lineage, so
every further step was refused and the objective stayed quarantined.

A contract input with no stored lineage is again accepted as released
custody only when the authenticated L1 source shows it carrying this
objective's computation-thread token under a step datum whose
fraud_prover is the reservation's funding key. Any other output stays
refused.

Remove the convicted block under the deployment's finalized manifest

The installed validation-trace lifecycle now binds a finalized manifest
describing the scene's deployment as both the watcher identity and the
removal's deployment, so the convicted block's own removal and its
bond-backed slash are funded and land. The lifecycle test drives the run
to its terminal and checks the spent operator bond and the reward output.

Mark the deleted submission-handoff module as historical in two decision records

The module went when each funding change began committing with its journal
entries; the records keep the reference and say it no longer exists.

Slash a lost defender by its receipt once the dispute is settled

The validation-trace runner now slashes each defender who lost a thread of
our case, by that thread's lost-defense receipt, under the prover funding
permit. The slash is due only once the case is settled for us: after the
close when the defender won, and after the convicted block's removal when
the case convicted. It never precedes or blocks a thread move, the close or
the removal. A due slash that does not build holds the run under an alarm
naming its deadline, the defender's bond unlock, until it lands; when
another watcher lands it first the run stops cleanly.

The funding permit admits the slash only under an authority that binds its
exact receipt action, header, deployment, economics, operator bond input,
reward, fee, reward address and inputs.

The removal's raw-L1 terminal derivation accepts a block whose operator was
already slashed by this case's receipt, taking the bond's end from the one
transaction that burns that receipt and consumes the operator's bond.

New emulator tests cover the slash landing, another watcher landing it
first, the unbuilt alarm, every permit refusal, and the removal after the
operator's receipt slash.

Cover the shared watcher.sqlite writers with guard, contention and timing rows

The workflow journal refuses an entry out of sequence as a concurrent write and
keeps its rows; a funding change committed on one connection is read on another
rather than a cached audit. A prepare and its confirmation complete while the
durable state-queue backend appends and another process holds the write lock in
bursts on the same file. A prepared body of about 1.4 MB and 200 ordinary
entries commit within loose bounds, and the row logs both timings.

Drop the unused workflow-id listing from the workflow journal

Nothing reads every workflow id any more; the one test that did now asserts
the objective's single execution instead.

Keep two watcher modules within their size ceilings

The unattended-objective wiring had raised the ceilings of the progress
authority and the supervisor. Optional callbacks and retention are now
passed through directly, and the in-process job check reads one list, so
both modules fit their earlier ceilings again.

Delete a forgotten objective's workflow rows when its funding settles

A released objective whose execution holds a signed attempt is forgotten
with its workflow rows kept. The funding sweep that settles that attempt's
reservation, once each attempt is retired on L1, now deletes those rows in
the same watcher.sqlite transaction, so they no longer stay without limit.
An objective whose header returned before the sweep keeps its rows and its
funding for its run.

fault_proof_objective_unreadable stays: startup can still meet workflow
rows it cannot read (a corrupt row, a foreign execution, a storage error),
and holding that objective keeps startup from failing. The docs for it and
for fault_proof_objective_cleanup_failed, and the README's cleanup and
retention text, describe workflow rows instead of directories and
tombstones.
